title: Keep component pages' relevant-functions (title/href/signature) in sync with the shiny.ui API
description:
## Problem

Each component/layout doc page declares a `relevant-functions` listing block in its `index.qmd` front matter, e.g. `components/outputs/value-box/index.qmd`:

```yaml
- id: relevant-functions
  template: ../../_partials/components-detail-relevant-functions.ejs
  contents:
  - title: ui.value_box
    href: https://shiny.posit.co/py/api/ui.value_box.html
    signature: ui.value_box(title, value, *args, showcase=None, ...)
```

These three fields — `title`, `href`, and `signature` — are **hand-authored and never regenerated**. `components/migrate.py` performed only a one-time conversion from an older metadata format; there is no ongoing build step or check that keeps them aligned with the real `shiny.ui` / `shiny.express.ui` API.

Consequences:
- A `signature:` can silently drift from the actual function signature after an upstream py-shiny change.
- An `href:` can rot (e.g. an API page renamed/moved).
- A `title:` can name a function that no longer exists (a renamed/removed export).

## Existing partial backstop

`components/test_ui_api_has_page.py` was added to enforce that every public `ui` export is documented by a page (or explicitly opted out). Its `test_documented_functions_are_real_exports` guard already catches a `title:` that names a **nonexistent** `ui` export. It does **not** validate `href` or `signature`.

## Proposed work

Add a check (unit test and/or build step) that, for every `relevant-functions` entry across `components/**/index.qmd` and `layouts/**/index.qmd`:

1. **`signature`** matches the live signature of the named function (via `inspect.signature`, formatted to match the existing convention — note entries use `MISSING`/`...` sentinels and wrapped lines, so normalize before comparing, or regenerate rather than compare).
2. **`href`** resolves to a real API reference page (at minimum, that the target `api/**` file is generated; optionally an HTTP check for the canonical shiny.posit.co URL).
3. **`title`** names a real export (already covered by `test_ui_api_has_page.py::test_documented_functions_are_real_exports` — consolidate here or cross-reference).

Consider whether it's better to **generate** these fields from the API at build time (single source of truth) rather than lint hand-written values. Generation would eliminate drift entirely; a lint keeps authoring flexible but requires the normalization above.

## Pointers

- Front-matter block + EJS template: `_partials/components-detail-relevant-functions.ejs`
- One-time migration (not a generator): `components/migrate.py` (see `relevantFunctions` handling, ~lines 46, 130-140)
- Related coverage test: `components/test_ui_api_has_page.py`
- API surface: `shiny.ui.__all__`, `shiny.express.ui.__all__`

title: test: widen example-app page-coverage enforcement beyond accordion
description:
The example-app page-coverage check (`components/test_component_pages.py`) discovers every component page (`components/<section>/<name>/index.qmd`) but only **enforces** that a page ships at least one example app (`app.py` / `app-*.py`) for the pages listed in `ENFORCE_HAS_APP` — currently just `layout/accordion`. This was intentionally narrowed so the initial testing PR (#398) could land without requiring every page to have an example app immediately.

- Add more `<section>/<name>` paths to `ENFORCE_HAS_APP` as pages gain example apps, **or**

title: Smoke tests: two example apps need a newer shiny than the pinned py-shiny submodule
description:
The example-app smoke tests (`test-smoke` workflow / `make test-smoke`) launch each
`components/**/app-*.py` against the `shiny` installed from the **pinned py-shiny
submodule** (currently `v1.6.3`). Two example apps use APIs newer than that version,
so they fail the smoke sweep. They are **temporarily made to pass** in
`components/test_examples_smoke.py` (referencing this issue) so CI stays green.

### Failing apps (temporarily whitelisted / xfailed)

1. **`display-messages/chat/app-preview.py`** — uses the deprecated
   `ui.Chat(messages=...)` (deprecated in favor of `chat.ui(messages=...)`). It emits a
   `ShinyDeprecationWarning` on stderr, and the smoke checker treats deprecation warnings
   as errors unless whitelisted. *Temp fix:* the deprecation is whitelisted for this app.

2. **`outputs/verbatim-text/app-variation-placeholder-rectangle-when-string-is-empty-express.py`**
   — uses `shiny.express.ui.output_text_verbatim(..., placeholder=True)`, which does not
   exist in shiny `1.6.3` (Express gained explicit `ui.output_*` functions in a later
   release). *Temp fix:* the app is `xfail`ed.

### Root cause

The submodule-pinned `shiny` is older than the runtime the live shinylive examples target,
so a few examples reference not-yet-available / since-deprecated APIs.

### To resolve

- Bump the py-shiny submodule to a version that ships these APIs, **and** update the chat
  example to the non-deprecated `chat.ui(messages=...)` form.
- Then remove the corresponding entries from `ALLOW_STDERR` / `XFAIL` in
  `components/test_examples_smoke.py`.

title: Make the Variation Showcase (kitchen-sink) image link to the Express shinylive app
description:
## Summary

On component pages, the **Variation Showcase** (kitchen-sink) block renders a static screenshot (`thumbnail.png`) followed by two buttons — **Live Core App** / **Live Express App** — that link to the full shinylive editor. The screenshot itself is a bare image and is **not** clickable.

We should make the Showcase image itself a link (to the Express shinylive app) so clicking the screenshot opens the live app, matching the intuition that the preview image is interactive.

## Where

Shared partial used by every component page:

`components/_partials/components-detail-kitchen-sink.ejs`

```
![](<%= item.image %>){.border .my-4 style="border-radius: .5em;"}
```

## Proposed change

Wrap the image in a link to the Express app URL:

```diff
-![](<%= item.image %>){.border .my-4 style="border-radius: .5em;"}
+[![](<%= item.image %>){.border .my-4 style="border-radius: .5em;"}](<%= item.express %>){target="_blank"}
```

(Open question: link to `item.express` or `item.core`? Core is the left-most/primary tab elsewhere, so it may be the more consistent target — decide during implementation.)

## Scope / impact

This partial is shared by **all** component pages (~40), so this is a site-wide rendering change, not scoped to a single component. It should land in its own PR. The two existing buttons already provide the links, so this is a UX/affordance improvement rather than a functional fix.

## Context

Surfaced while reviewing the Accordion component page (PR #391). The Showcase links themselves work; this is purely about making the screenshot a clickable affordance.

title: Retire local shinylive cache patch once quarto-ext/shinylive#80 ships
description:
The vendored shinylive extension carries a local performance patch (subprocess render cache, added in #382; kept as `scripts/patches/shinylive-cache.patch` and re-applied by `make quarto-extensions`). The same optimization is proposed upstream: quarto-ext/shinylive#79 (issue) / quarto-ext/shinylive#80 (draft PR).

Once the upstream PR merges and a release ships:

1. `make clean-extensions quarto-extensions` — the patch re-apply will fail loudly against the new upstream; that's the signal to retire it rather than re-port.
2. Delete `scripts/patches/shinylive-cache.patch` and the patch-apply block in the Makefile's `_extensions/quarto-ext/shinylive` target.
3. Keep the `shinylive-assets` ensure step in `make site`/`serve` unless upstream ensures assets itself (see the asset-download side-effect discussion in quarto-ext/shinylive#79).
4. Remove the patch notes from CLAUDE.md and README.
5. Verify: local render still hits the (now upstream) cache, and a CI run on a PR stays in the ~12 min range.

If upstream lands with different cache-key/invalidations semantics, sanity-check that `.quarto/shinylive-cache` persistence in `.github/workflows/deploy-docs.yml` still matches (path + the requirements.txt-hash cache key).

title: docs: Document test mode in the end-to-end testing article
description:
Companion to posit-dev/py-shiny#2284 (test mode shipped in posit-dev/py-shiny#2270, snapshot preprocessing in posit-dev/py-shiny#2282; api-examples added in the py-shiny PR that closes that issue).

py-shiny now has a **test mode**, but the site's testing docs (`docs/end-to-end-testing.qmd`, `docs/unit-testing.qmd`) don't mention it. Add a section to `docs/end-to-end-testing.qmd` (or a short new article) covering:

## What to document

1. **Enabling test mode** — `App(test_mode=True)` or the `SHINY_TESTMODE=1` env var. The pytest app-launch fixtures (`local_app`, `create_app_fixture`) enable it by default, so most test authors get it for free.
2. **Exporting internal reactive values** — `shiny.testmode.export_test_values(name=callable)` in the server function surfaces reactive values (e.g. a `reactive.calc`) in the snapshot's `export` block. It's a no-op outside test mode, so calls can be left in production code.
3. **Reading the snapshot in a test** — the `shiny.playwright.controller.AppTestValues` controller: `expect_input()` / `expect_output()` / `expect_export()` (per-key, auto-retrying), `expect_inputs()` / `expect_outputs()` / `expect_exports()` (whole-block, `match="subset"|"exact"`), and `get()` for the raw `{"input": ..., "output": ..., "export": ...}` dict.
4. **Snapshot preprocessing** (scrubbing nondeterministic/sensitive values) — `shiny.testmode.snapshot_preprocess_input(id, fn)` (or `input.set_snapshot_preprocess(...)`) for inputs, and `my_output.snapshot_preprocess(fn)` on a `@render.*` object for outputs. File inputs automatically scrub `datapath` to the basename.
5. (Optional, advanced) the raw snapshot endpoint `/session/{id}/dataobj/shinytest` and `session.get_test_snapshot_url()`, including the `?input=`/`?output=`/`?export=` block-selection query params.

## Ready-made source material

- Example apps in py-shiny: `shiny/api-examples/export_test_values/` and `shiny/api-examples/snapshot_preprocess_input/` (core + express variants).
- A complete end-to-end test exercising all of the above: `tests/playwright/shiny/test_mode/` (app + test) in py-shiny.
- API reference docstrings: `shiny/testmode.py` and `shiny/playwright/controller/_app_test_values.py`.

A minimal end-to-end example for the article:

```python
# app.py
from shiny import App, Inputs, Outputs, Session, reactive, render, ui
from shiny.testmode import export_test_values

app_ui = ui.page_fluid(
    ui.input_slider("n", "N", min=0, max=100, value=20),
    ui.output_text_verbatim("txt"),
)

def server(input: Inputs, output: Outputs, session: Session):
    @reactive.calc
    def doubled():
        return input.n() * 2

    @render.text
    def txt():
        return f"n * 2 = {doubled()}"

    export_test_values(doubled=doubled)

app = App(app_ui, server)
```

```python
# test_app.py
from playwright.sync_api import Page

from shiny.playwright import controller
from shiny.run import ShinyAppProc

def test_doubled(page: Page, local_app: ShinyAppProc) -> None:
    page.goto(local_app.url)

    app_values = controller.AppTestValues(page)
    app_values.expect_export("doubled", 40)

    controller.InputSlider(page, "n").set("30")
    app_values.expect_export("doubled", 60)
```

title: [bug]Theme examples missing on deployed site due to case-sensitive filesystem (api-examples/theme vs Theme)
description:
## Summary

The `express.ui.Theme` (and `ui.Theme`) API docs show an **Examples** section locally on macOS but not on the deployed Linux build.

## Root Cause

`@add_example()` in py-shiny uses `func.__name__` to locate the example directory:

```python
fn_name = func.__name__   # → "Theme" (capital T)
example_dir = os.path.join(ex_dir_found, fn_name)  # → api-examples/Theme/
```

But the actual directory on disk is `shiny/api-examples/theme/` (lowercase `t`).

- **macOS** — case-insensitive filesystem: `api-examples/Theme/` resolves to `api-examples/theme/` ✅ example found
- **Linux CI** — case-sensitive filesystem: `api-examples/Theme/` does not exist → `ExampleNotFoundException` is caught silently, a `::warning` is printed, and `@add_example()` returns without modifying the docstring → **no Examples section generated**

The silent failure is in `_docstring.py`:

```python
except ExampleNotFoundException as e:
    print(f"::warning file={file},...::{fn_name} - {e}")
    return func  # ← silently skips the example
```

## Evidence

- The warning can be observed in the CI logs for the last `main` build:  
  https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny-site/actions/runs/23913127706
- The fix should live in the **py-shiny** repo: either rename `api-examples/theme/` → `api-examples/Theme/`, or change `@add_example()` to do a case-insensitive directory lookup.

## Affected Pages

- `/api/express/express.ui.Theme.html`
- `/api/core/ui.Theme.html`

## Notes

This is a latent bug that exists on `main` today — not introduced by the Quarto 1.9 upgrade. It is visible now because the local (macOS) build is being compared against the deployed (Linux) build.

title: [BUG] Caret drifts to the right on the same line in express.ui.input_code_editor (Shiny 1.6.0)
description:
### Description

I’m seeing a caret / cursor rendering issue with `express.ui.input_code_editor` in Shiny 1.6.0.
**This appears immediately on the official examples on [shiny.posit.co](http://shiny.posit.co/) as well, so it does not seem to be specific to my local app.**
https://shiny.posit.co/py/api/express/express.ui.input_code_editor.html

The problem is most noticeable when continuing to type on the same line. As I keep typing, the caret gradually drifts to the right and becomes visually separated from the actual text insertion point.

If I press Enter and move to a new line, the caret alignment looks correct again at first. But while typing continuously on that new line, the same drift starts happening again.

So this seems to be a line-level caret positioning issue that accumulates while typing on a single line.

### Environment

- Shiny: 1.6.0
- Windows, Google Chrome


Click into the code editor.

Type continuously on a single line.

Observe that the caret gradually shifts farther to the right than the actual text position.

Press Enter to go to the next line.

Notice that the caret alignment looks normal again initially.

Continue typing on that new line.

Observe that the drift starts again.

Expected behavior:
The caret should stay visually aligned with the true insertion point while typing, regardless of how long the current line is.


Actual behavior:
When typing continuously on the same line, the caret gradually drifts to the right and becomes visibly separated from the text. Pressing Enter temporarily resets the alignment, but the issue reappears as typing continues on the new line.

title: Plotly compatibility issue causing deployment failures on shinyapps.io (JSON serialization errors)
description:
Description
Summary

During deployment of a PyShiny application to shinyapps.io, we encountered runtime failures related to Plotly compatibility, despite the application working correctly in local development. The issue was traced to a conflict with newer versions of Plotly when used together with shinywidgets / FigureWidget.

Pinning Plotly to a previous stable version resolves the problem.

Environment

Platform: shinyapps.io

OS (local dev): Windows

Python: 3.11

shiny: 1.1.0

shinywidgets: 0.3.3

plotly (failing): latest available at deploy time

plotly (working): 5.24.1

Observed behavior

Application deploys successfully but fails at runtime.

Errors occur when rendering Plotly outputs via shinywidgets (FigureWidget).

Typical errors include:

TypeError: datetime.date(...) is not JSON serializable

Failures during widget serialization (json.dumps) inside shinywidgets

Errors appear both during initial render and reactive updates.

Expected behavior

Plotly figures rendered via shinywidgets should serialize and render correctly in shinyapps.io, including figures that contain date-based axes or data.

Root cause analysis

The issue appears to be caused by incompatibilities between newer Plotly versions and the current serialization pipeline used by shinywidgets / ipywidgets.
Specifically:

datetime.date objects embedded in Plotly figure data are not automatically converted to JSON-safe formats.

This causes failures during widget state synchronization between Python and the browser.

Workaround / Resolution

Pinning Plotly to a stable, known-compatible version resolves the issue:

plotly==5.24.1


After pinning Plotly (and redeploying), the application runs correctly on shinyapps.io without serialization errors.

Additional notes

The same codebase works locally and in deployment once Plotly is pinned.

This suggests a regression or behavioral change in recent Plotly releases affecting widget-based rendering.

description:
## Problem

In the Learn Shiny section of our website, the page titles are, e.g.

* [Shiny for Python - Dynamic UI](https://shiny.posit.co/py/docs/ui-dynamic.html)
* [Shiny for Python - Patterns](https://shiny.posit.co/py/docs/ui-dynamic.html)

* [Shiny Components](https://shiny.posit.co/py/components/)
* [Shiny Layouts](https://shiny.posit.co/py/layouts/)
* [Shiny Templates](https://shiny.posit.co/py/templates/)

## Suggestion

I think it'd be better to have the page title move from most to least specific:

* Components - Shiny for Python
* Layouts - Shiny for Python
* Templates - Shiny for Python

In the case of Learn Shiny, we might even want to include the parent section in the page title:

* Dynamic UI - User Interfaces - Shiny for Python
* Patterns - Reactivity - Shiny for Python

This ordering helps those of us with many tabs open (a.k.a. all of us) making it easier to see at a glance which page is in each tab. Note that it's clear which pages are shiny-related because of the favicon.

title: Future state of Shiny Extends
description:
I went through our JS template process and ran into some documentation/template issues. I think these are bigger jobs which shouldn't block #46, so thought I'd break them out here:

# Documentation 
There are explanations and how-tos that we need to include here. IMO they are:
## Explanation
- An overview of how Shiny works:
   - Adding HTML dependenceis
   - A high level picture of how data flows from the UI to the server and back again
- Inputs
    - What is an input binding and how does it work?
- Outputs
    - Rendering decorators
    - Output bindings
- JS best practices
    - Web components and why we use them
    - TypeScript and why we use it

## How to
I think this should be broken down into a few cases:

1) Including JavaScript in your app 
2) Building a package with a JS input
3) Building a package with a JS output
4) Building a React based package with both inputs and outputs
5) (Later, building a Vue extension, or a Svelte extension)

## Appendix
- What do the files in the template mean and do?


# Template changes
I found it difficult to build a React output based on our current template because the output boilerplate wasn't included. I think we should include both inputs and outputs for each template because it's much easier to delete the boilerplate code than to find and add it. This would also reduce the number of templates we need because we wouldn't need an input/output one.  The template structure for each JS framework would be something like:

```
example-apps
      - input-app.py
      - output-app.py
my-component
      - my-component-input.py
      - my-component-output.py
 scrts
      - index.tsx (include both input and output Javascript)
```

Out templates would then match the framework and include both Input and Output bindings:
- JS template
- React template
- Vue template
- Svelte template

title: Offcanvas has no doc page: test_every_ui_export_has_a_page fails on shiny 1.7.0
description:
Surfaced by #421, which updates the py-shiny submodule to v1.7.0. The `apps (1)` job fails:

```
FAILED components/test_ui_api_has_page.py::test_every_ui_export_has_a_page
AssertionError: These shiny.ui / shiny.express.ui exports have no doc page:
  ['Offcanvas', 'hide_offcanvas', 'offcanvas', 'show_offcanvas', 'toggle_offcanvas'].
```

Job: https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny-site/actions/runs/30425246143/job/90490193349

## Cause

shiny 1.7.0 added the Offcanvas component (posit-dev/py-shiny#2279) — a sliding Bootstrap Offcanvas panel that enters from a viewport edge. Five new public exports arrived with it:

| Export | What it is |
|---|---|
| `offcanvas()` | creates the panel |
| `show_offcanvas()` | reveals it programmatically |
| `hide_offcanvas()` | hides it by id |
| `toggle_offcanvas()` | toggles it by id |
| `Offcanvas` | the class |

`test_every_ui_export_has_a_page` computes `API - DOCUMENTED - KNOWN_MISSING_COMPONENTS`, so any new `shiny.ui` export fails the build until it is either documented or explicitly opted out. This is the test doing its job — the site genuinely has no Offcanvas documentation yet.

## Fix

Per the assertion's own guidance, either:

1. **Write the page** (preferred) — add a `components/` page for Offcanvas and list the five exports in its `relevant-functions` front-matter block. Being a panel triggered by a UI element and controllable by id, it sits naturally alongside the existing popover/tooltip/modal pages, and those are a good template for the show/hide/toggle mutator pattern.

title: Auto-generate kitchen-sink core/express shinylive URLs (2 of 40 are already stale)
description:
The `kitchen-sink` block's `core:` / `express:` values are full Shinylive **editor** URLs that encode the app source, exactly like the `shinylive:` values on the example apps — but unlike those, nothing regenerates them and no CI check verifies them. They are hand-maintained, so they rot silently.

`.claude/skills/writing-component-pages/SKILL.md` documents this as intended:

> Kitchen-sink `core`/`express` URLs are full `.../editor/#h=0&code=...` links added by hand (they open the full editor), not generated by the script.

## This has already bitten us

I decoded all 40 committed kitchen-sink URLs (20 pages × core/express) and compared each against its `app-kitchensink-*.py` on disk. **38 match; 2 are stale** — both on `components/layout/accordion/`:

```diff
# layout/accordion, core: decoded URL vs app-kitchensink-core.py
-            ui.output_text_verbatim("result"),
+            ui.output_code("result"),
-    ui.output_text_verbatim("open_panels"),
+    ui.output_code("open_panels"),
-    @render.text
+    @render.code

# layout/accordion, express: decoded URL vs app-kitchensink-express.py
-        @render.text
+        @render.code
```

The accordion kitchen-sink apps were migrated from `output_text_verbatim` / `@render.text` to `output_code` / `@render.code`, but their editor URLs were never regenerated. **The "Open in editor" links on that page still serve the pre-migration code.** Note the express URL is even the *same length* as the current file (764 == 764 chars) — this is not something a reviewer will ever spot by eye.

## Why it happens

`components/update-shinylive-links.py` walks each `index.qmd` and rewrites `shinylive:` keys, but it has no kitchen-sink handling — `grep -n 'kitchen' components/update-shinylive-links.py` returns nothing. So:

- `make components-shinylive-links` does not touch these URLs, and
- the `test-shinylive-links` CI workflow, which regenerates links and fails on any diff, gives them **zero** coverage.

Every kitchen sink added is new unverified surface. Concretely relevant right now: the docs PRs for #409 are adding new inputs pages, and kitchen sinks are the natural home for the parameters those pages don't otherwise demonstrate.

## The shape is already uniform, so this is easy

All 20 kitchen-sink blocks follow one convention with **zero** exceptions — one `core:`, one `express:`, one `image:`, no `resources:`, and both `app-kitchensink-core.py` and `app-kitchensink-express.py` plus `thumbnail.png` present in the page dir. So the mapping is unambiguous:

| front-matter key | source file |
|---|---|
| `core:` | `app-kitchensink-core.py` |
| `express:` | `app-kitchensink-express.py` |

## Proposal

Teach `components/update-shinylive-links.py` to rewrite the `kitchen-sink` entry's `core`/`express` values from those two files, so `make components-shinylive-links` covers them and `test-shinylive-links` starts failing when they drift.

The encoding is scriptable — verified locally:

```python
import shinylive
payload = shinylive.url_encode(path, language="py", mode="editor").split("code=", 1)[1]
url = f"https://shinylive.io/py/editor/#h=0&code={payload}"
```

Two implementation notes:

1. **`h=0` must be prepended manually.** `shinylive.url_encode`'s `header` argument is only honored when `mode="app"`, so it won't emit `h=0` for editor mode. The existing committed URLs all carry `h=0` (no header chrome), so preserve that.
2. **The first regeneration will produce a diff on all 20 pages, even the 38 URLs that are semantically correct.** Current shinylive adds a `"type"` field to each file object in the payload that older releases didn't, so the compressed strings differ even when the decoded content is byte-identical. That's expected churn, not a bug — worth landing as its own commit so it doesn't obscure the two real fixes.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `make components-shinylive-links` regenerates kitchen-sink `core`/`express` URLs
- [ ] `FILES=` scoping works for them like it does for `shinylive:` keys
- [ ] `test-shinylive-links` fails when a committed kitchen-sink URL is stale
- [ ] `layout/accordion`'s two stale URLs are corrected
- [ ] SKILL.md:205 updated — drop "added by hand", document the generator instead

title: relevant-functions hrefs are absolute to production, so previews link off-site
description:
## Summary

`relevant-functions` hrefs on every component and layout page are **absolute URLs to production docs**. They should be site-relative (or at least root-relative `/py/api/...`) so a page links to the API docs built alongside it.

`components/_relevant_functions.py` L23 hard-codes:

```python
API_BASE_URL = "https://shiny.posit.co/py/api/core"
```

and `_href()` (L97-98) builds `{base}/{stem}.html#{anchor}`.

## Why it matters

In a PR preview (`pr-123--pyshiny.netlify.app`), every `relevant-functions` link navigates the reader **off the preview and onto the live site**. So:

- you cannot review a component page's API links in a preview — you are reviewing production's copy of them
- a PR that adds or renames an API page cannot demonstrate its own links resolving
- a submodule bump that changes an anchor looks fine in preview and breaks on deploy

Same problem for anyone building or serving the site locally.

## Scope

Two related pieces of cleanup; worth doing together since both are "hrefs pointing at the wrong place":

**1. The generated `relevant-functions` hrefs (~113 of them).**
Change `API_BASE_URL` to a root-relative base and regenerate with `make components-relevant-functions`. Note the `test-relevant-functions` CI check compares committed values against generated ones, so the generator change and the bulk regeneration must land in the same commit.

Decide relative vs root-relative: `/py/api/core/...` is simpler and correct for every deployment of this site, but hard-codes the `/py` prefix. Truly relative hrefs (`../../../api/core/...`) survive any prefix but vary by page depth, so the generator has to compute them from the page's own path. Root-relative is probably the right trade — the `/py` prefix is already assumed throughout `_quarto.yml`.

**2. Five legacy body links that omit the `core/` segment** (was tracked separately as F-12):

- `layouts/panels-cards/index.qmd:246`
- `layouts/arrange/index.qmd:212, 226, 249`

These are `/py/api/ui.*.html` and currently **work** — they 301-redirect to `/py/api/core/...` — so this half is cosmetic: one redirect hop, and inconsistent with the `relevant-functions` blocks on the same pages. Normalize them in the same sweep.

## Verification

After regenerating, spot-check a preview build that the links resolve **within** the preview rather than to `shiny.posit.co`, and confirm anchors still land (the `#shiny.<qualified-name>` fragments must survive the base change unchanged).

Split out from the SKILL.md href-format fix that shipped in #417 — that corrected the *documented* format; this changes the format itself.

title: ci: the 10 site build shards are not gating merges (deploy skips instead of failing)
description:
## Summary

The ten `build (N)` shards in `site.yml` are almost certainly **not gating merges**, even though `deploy` is a required check.

## The gap

Required checks on `main` are:

```
deploy, done-test-apps, done-test-smoke, test-relevant-functions, test-shinylive-links
```

The individual `build (1..10)` jobs are **not** required — `deploy` is expected to cover them via `needs: build`. But `.github/workflows/site.yml` L81-82 declares it with no `if:`:

```yaml
  deploy:
    needs: build
```

With a plain `needs:` and no `if: always()`, a failing upstream job makes the dependent job **skip** rather than fail. And GitHub treats a skipped required check as **satisfied**.

This repo already documents that exact footgun, twice — `.github/workflows/test-apps.yml` L46-48:

```yaml
    # `always()` is required: without it, a failing shard would make this job
    # skip, and GitHub treats a skipped required check as satisfied.
    if: always()
```

`done-test-apps` and `done-test-smoke` were written correctly (`if: always()` plus an explicit `failure|cancelled|skipped` result check). The `build` matrix never got the same treatment.

Net effect: a broken site render likely leaves the PR mergeable — for the most expensive check in the pipeline, and the only one that actually renders the site.

## Evidence level — please confirm before relying on this either way

- **Certain:** a failing `build` shard causes `deploy` to be skipped. That follows directly from GitHub Actions `needs:` semantics.
- **Not independently confirmed here:** that a skipped `deploy` then counts as a *satisfied* required check. That half rests on the premise this repo documents twice, not on an end-to-end test.
- No run history to check against: the only failed `site.yml` run ([30562090704](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny-site/actions/runs/30562090704)) had all 10 shards green with `deploy` itself failing — which *does* block correctly, and so does not exercise the case in question.

The cheap confirmation is a throwaway PR that deliberately breaks one shard, then reading the mergeability state.

## Fix

Mirror what the other two sharded workflows already do:

1. Add a `done-build` aggregator with `if: always()`, `needs: build`, and a `failure|cancelled|skipped` check over `needs.*.result` — same shape as `done-test-apps`.
2. Add `done-build` to the required-checks list.
3. Stop requiring `deploy` (it does not run on all events and is not the right gate), **or** additionally give `deploy` `if: always()` plus an explicit upstream-result check.

Option 1 + 2 is preferred: it matches the existing pattern, and the required-check name stays stable if the shard count changes — which was the original reason for the `done-*` jobs in #425.

title: great-tables: Shinylive examples run 0.21.x while tests assert against 0.23.0 (multimark blocks Pyodide)
description:
## Summary

The Great Tables page's Shinylive examples run a **different, older** `great-tables` than its tests assert against.

- `components/outputs/table-great-tables/requirements.txt` pins `great-tables<0.22` → readers get **0.21.x** in the browser
- the test venv resolves **0.23.0**, which is what `test_great_tables.py` asserts formatted values against

Harmless today (the assertions hold in both), but the two will drift, and a formatting change in either direction produces a confusing failure — or worse, passing tests that describe output no reader sees.

## Why the ceiling exists

`great-tables` **0.22.0** added a hard dependency on `multimark`, which publishes only compiled platform wheels (cp39–cp313) and no `py3-none-any`. micropip cannot install it under Pyodide. Verified in a real browser on shinylive.io:

- unpinned → `ValueError: Can't find a pure Python 3 wheel for 'multimark>=0.1.3'`, app pane shows **"Error starting app!"**
- `<0.22` → table renders fully, 0 console errors

So the pin is load-bearing and must not be casually removed. (It has been removed and reverted once already — see #389.)

## Tasks

1. **Investigate why `multimark` cannot install under Pyodide, and whether that is fixable.** This is the actual blocker and it is upstream of us. Questions worth answering:
   - Is `multimark` a compiled extension by necessity, or is it pure Python that merely *ships* as platform wheels? If the latter, a `py3-none-any` wheel is a small upstream ask.
   - Is the dependency optional in practice — i.e. does `great-tables` need it for the code paths our examples use? If so, ask upstream to make it an extra.
   - Failing both: is `multimark` a candidate for the Pyodide package set?
   
   File upstream (`posit-dev/great-tables`, and/or `multimark`) with findings and link back here.
2. **Close the gap in the meantime.** Options, cheapest first:
   - pin the *test* environment to the same range the examples get, so tests assert what readers see; or
   - keep versions split but make the assertions version-tolerant (e.g. regex rather than exact `$421,000` / `33.0%`).
3. **Add a guard.** Nothing currently detects that a pinned range has stopped installing under Pyodide — that failure is silent until someone loads the page. A CI check that the pinned requirements resolve in Pyodide would catch it. Related to #424, which wants generated/verified Shinylive URLs.

Two footguns for whoever picks this up: Great Tables renders a **Unicode minus (U+2212)**, not an ASCII hyphen, so `-3.0%` never matches; and `InputSlider.set()` needs the comma-formatted tick label (`"300,000"`, not `"300000"`).

title: docs: adopt kitchen-sink apps beyond the inputs section (orphan parameters have no home)
description:
## Summary

Kitchen-sink apps (`app-kitchensink-{core,express}.py`) are effectively an **inputs-section-only** convention today. That leaves parameters on the other sections' pages named in prose but never demonstrated anywhere.

Current distribution:

| section | pages with a kitchen sink |
|---|---|
| inputs | **20 / 24** |
| outputs | 1 / 15 (`value-box`) |
| display-messages | **0 / 7** |
| layout | 1 / 3 (`accordion`) |

`.claude/skills/writing-component-pages/SKILL.md` marks the kitchen sink `# optional`, so this is a convention gap, not a rule violation. But the consequence is concrete.

## Consequence: orphan parameters

A parameter that has no kitchen sink and no dedicated variation gets a prose mention and nothing more — no runnable demo, no test, and no protection against the API changing under it. Known instances:

- **popover** — `options` (never shown); 3 of 5 `placement` values never render
- **toasts** — 4 of 9 `type` values and 4 of 9 `position` values never render
- **code** — `output_code(placeholder=False)` named but never shown
- **table** — `render.table(index=, classes=, border=, **kwargs)`: two of four named
- **markdown-stream** — `content_type="html"`, `clear=False` append, `auto_scroll=False` all merely named

## Proposal

Adopt kitchen sinks across **all** component pages, so every documented parameter has at least one place it is actually exercised. This also gives the smoke sweep something to run for each parameter, which is how several real bugs in this batch were caught.

## Please decide these first

1. **Static previews** — display-messages pages deliberately omit `appPreview.static: true`, because a static render never runs the server and would show only a closed trigger button. A kitchen sink there needs the same treatment (live card, no thumbnail), or a different presentation.
2. **Rot surface** — kitchen-sink `core:`/`express:` URLs are full editor links that **nothing regenerates**; `make components-shinylive-links` does not handle the `kitchen-sink` listing id, so `test-shinylive-links` does not cover them. 2 of the existing 40 are already stale. **This should almost certainly land after #424**, otherwise every page added here is new unverified rot surface.
3. **Ordering** — worth doing outputs first (15 pages, most orphan parameters) and display-messages last (needs the static-preview question answered).

Blocked on / closely related to #424.

title: docs: accessibility guidance missing on 5 of 7 display-messages pages
description:
## Summary

Accessibility guidance appears on only **2 of 7** display-messages component pages.

| page | a11y coverage |
|---|---|
| tooltips | yes (~4 mentions) |
| popovers | yes (~3 mentions, added in #412) |
| chat | **none** |
| modal | **none** |
| notifications | **none** |
| progress-bar | **none** |
| toasts | **none** |

This is the component family where accessibility matters most — every one of these interrupts the user or announces something — so the gap is worth closing deliberately rather than page by page.

## Why these five in particular

Each has real, specific a11y surface that a reader cannot guess:

- **modal** — focus trapping and focus restoration on close; `Esc` dismissal; where focus lands on open.
- **notifications** / **toasts** — live-region announcement semantics. Whether these are announced by a screen reader at all, and whether `type=` maps to an appropriate role (`status` vs `alert`), determines whether a "success"/"error" message is perceivable non-visually. Toast `duration_s` auto-dismissal is also an a11y question: content that disappears on a timer.
- **progress-bar** — `aria-valuenow` / `aria-valuetext` and whether progress updates are announced.
- **chat** — streaming content in a live region; how partial tokens are announced.

## Suggested approach

1. Establish what the underlying bslib/Bootstrap components actually do — several of these get correct roles for free, and saying so is itself useful. py-shiny docstrings cover some of it.
2. Add a short, consistent "Accessibility" subsection to the five pages, modelled on the Tooltips page's treatment.
3. Where behavior is *not* handled automatically and the author must do something (e.g. choosing `type=` deliberately for `alert` semantics, or not relying solely on a timed toast), say so explicitly.

Do not add boilerplate — a paragraph that says nothing specific is worse than nothing, because it implies the topic has been handled.

title: docs(popovers): placement="right" example renders bottom (short-body Popper collision)
description:
## Summary

The Popovers page demonstrates `placement="right"`, but in the embedded example the popover renders **below** the trigger, not to its right. The parameter the example exists to show is not visible in the example.

`placement` is working correctly — this is a docs/example problem, not a Shiny bug. Details below, since the cause is non-obvious and worth recording.

## Reproduce

`components/display-messages/popovers/app-core.py` as shipped. Click the button, inspect the popover:

```
bslib-popover placement="right"          <- requested
.popover data-popper-placement="bottom"  <- actual
```

## Root cause

Popper's overflow check uses the page `<body>` as the boundary. The example app's body contains only the button, so it is **47px tall**, while the popover is **76px tall**. A `right`-placed popover therefore overflows the boundary vertically, and Popper falls back to `bottom`.

Bisected with two otherwise-identical apps at a 1600x900 viewport:

| app | body height | resolved placement |
|---|---|---|
| popover alone at top of page | 47px | `bottom` ❌ |
| same + a `height: 300px` spacer above it | 347px | `right` ✅ |

So the trigger having ~1400px of free space to its right is irrelevant — the collision is on the *vertical* axis. (This corrects an earlier internal note that concluded "not collision fallback"; it is collision fallback, just not on the axis you'd expect.)

## Fix

Give the example enough vertical room that the requested placement survives — e.g. wrap the trigger so the body is taller than the popover, or place the popover mid-page. Confirmed sufficient: a 300px spacer.

Once the example actually shows `right`, `test_popovers.py` can also assert it via `controller.Popover.expect_placement()`, which it currently and deliberately does not.

## Docs note

The current prose is accurate and should stay:

> `placement` is a preference rather than a guarantee: the popover is repositioned automatically when there isn't room where you asked for it.

It may be worth adding that "room" is evaluated against the containing document, so a very short page can defeat the requested placement — this surprises people in exactly the short-demo-app case.

Worth checking the Tooltips page for the same issue (same overlay base class).

Found while reviewing #412. Verified against `shiny` 1.7.1.dev6.
